tier_reason: The README's Performance Status section says MarshalJSON and UnmarshalJSON are each '2x to 3x' faster than encoding/json. It gives no Go version, CPU, or results table. The repo does contain benchmark code against encoding/json: tests/goser/goser_test.go, tests/go.stripe/stripe_test.go, and the Makefile 'bench' target. That makes this first-party evidence with partial methodology, so it is tier C, not A or B.

corrections.caveats: The README says only '2x to 3x' faster than encoding/json. It gives no results table, Go version, or hardware. Benchmark code does exist: tests/goser and tests/go.stripe each have BenchmarkMarshalJSON/BenchmarkFFMarshalJSON/BenchmarkUnmarshalJSON/BenchmarkFFUnmarshalJSON, run by 'make bench'. The 2014 launch blog post gives 1.91x (goser) and 2.11x (go.stripe) for Marshal only, because Unmarshal did not exist yet. It states no Go version or hardware. A third-party table in the easyjson README (go1.6, Feb 2016, no CPU stated) measures ffjson against encoding/json. Unmarshal: 66 vs 22 MB/s regular (~3.0x) and 17.6 vs 9.7 MB/s small (~1.8x). Marshal: 122 vs 75 (~1.6x), 36 vs 32 (~1.1x) and 134 vs 80 MB/s large (~1.7x). Those ratios are derived from page data, so marshal gains were below the README's 2-3x there. ffjson falls back to encoding/json for interface members, custom marshalers, complex map values, and some nested slices/inline structs. The README warns that with interfaces it 'may even become slower than using json.Marshal directly'. The last commit on master is 2019-09-30 (repo pushed_at 2023-09-21 has no matching commit on any branch), so all numbers predate many encoding/json improvements.

notes: The benchmark URL (README) matches the claimed_speedup exactly. The record's last_commit (2023-09-21) was the repo pushed_at timestamp, but the actual last commit on master is 2019-09-30, and no branch, tag, or release is newer. The record said there was no benchmark code, which is wrong, so caveats are corrected. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, not archived, not a fork. The status stays abandoned.
